events.content:
The build reproduces the problem exactly, and Next.js names it precisely:

> `connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route from being prerendered, blocking the page load

`/product` has no static shell at all. Because `await getInventory()` sits directly in the page body and calls `connection()`, the *entire* page — title included — is blocked on per-request data. Nothing can be prerendered, so navigation waits on the whole render before showing anything.

Of the three fixes Next.js suggests, `"use cache"` is out (the error notes it doesn't apply to `connection()`, since that's inherently per-request), and `instant = false` just sanctions the blocking behavior you're asking me to remove. Streaming is the right one: hoist the title into a prerenderable shell and move the data access into a child under `<Suspense>`.

Clean — that's just the harness, no stray servers.

## What was wrong

`/product` had **no static shell at all**. `await getInventory()` sat directly in the page body, and `getInventory` calls `connection()`, which is inherently per-request. With `cacheComponents: true`, that made the whole route un-prerenderable — the `<h1>` was held hostage to the inventory fetch. The build didn't just run slowly, it **failed outright**:

> Route "/product": Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data during prerendering… `connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route from being prerendered, blocking the page load

## The fix

Next.js offered three routes; only one actually fits:

- ~~`"use cache"`~~ — the error explicitly excludes `connection()`, since it's per-request by definition
- ~~`export const instant = false`~~ — this just *sanctions* the blocking behavior you asked me to remove
- **`<Suspense>`** — the correct one

In `app/product/page.tsx:1` I moved the data access out of the page and into an `Inventory` child under a Suspense boundary. The critical part is that `ProductPage` is **no longer `async`** — it awaits nothing, so it renders synchronously into a prerendered shell. Leaving the `await` in the page body would have blocked the page no matter where the boundary went.

## Verified

`/product` went from build failure to `◐ Partial Prerender`, and I measured the real production stream rather than trusting the label:

```
  26.1 ms  h1 "Premium Widget"   ← first flush
  26.1 ms  fallback
  63.5 ms  inventory count       ← streams in later
  63.5 ms  price
```

The title is in the prerendered HTML on disk (`.next/server/app/product.html`), which is also what makes the home→product `<Link>` navigation instant: Next prefetches that shell, so the title paints on click while inventory streams.

The fallback renders two placeholder lines mirroring the real content's shape, so the title doesn't jump when the data lands.

Two notes, neither requiring action from you:

- **`tsconfig.json` is modified, but not by me** — `next build` rewrote it ("mandatory changes were made"), setting `jsx: react-jsx` and adding `.next/dev/types`. Next 16 requires both and re-applies them on every build. It had also reflowed every array into multi-line noise; I restored the compact formatting and confirmed a subsequent build leaves the file untouched, so the diff is down to just the two required values.
- **`.gitignore` covers neither `.next/` nor `next-env.d.ts`**, so my builds left them untracked in `git status`. Unusual for a Next project — worth adding, but I didn't touch it since it's outside what you asked. (`package.json`/`package-lock.json` were already modified before I started.)
